segments: The seventeenth period.
The Arab kings.
Isa, who was in Damascus,
to hasten and go besiege al-Afdal in Salkhad, his fortress.
Now al-Afdal heard,
and went out in haste from Salkhad,
and arrived at Aleppo to his brother al-Zahir.
And both of them went against Manbij, which belonged to al-Adil, and captured it;
and likewise they captured Qal'at Najm.
And they returned and came and encamped against Hama;
and Nasir al-Din, son of Taqi al-Din, gave them thirty thousand Tyrian dinars,
and they left him and went by way of Baalbek against Damascus.
And al-Afdal and al-Zahir made a pact with each other,
that when they took Damascus,
it should belong to Malik al-Afdal,
until they went and captured Egypt;
and then al-Afdal should hand over Damascus to al-Zahir,
and Egypt should belong to him.
And with this aim they waged war against Damascus.
And when they were close to capturing it,
Malik al-Zahir became jealous of his brother Malik al-Afdal,
and said to him:
"Damascus shall be mine,
and I will send my forces with you, so that you may go and take Egypt for yourself."
And al-Afdal said to him:
"You know that my mother and my household are at the doors of strangers in Homs,
because he brought them down from Salkhad,
and gave it to Zayn al-Din Qarajah, his father's servant,
to be an aid to him.
Therefore, I desire that you leave Damascus to me,
that these women may find shelter in it,
for it is also right for you to be zealous on their behalf,
until we take Egypt."
Malik al-Zahir, however, contended and would not agree.
And when the nobles saw the division between them,
they left them and went away,
some of them indeed to al-Adil,
and some of them entered Damascus.
Then both brothers came to an agreement,
and sent to Malik al-Adil, their uncle, and sued for peace.
And al-Adil gave to Malik al-Zahir, in addition to Aleppo, Manbij, Apamea, Kafr Tab, and some of the territory of Ma'arrat,
and he gave to Malik al-Afdal Samosata, Sarug, Resh'ayna, and Jumlin.
And Malik al-Adil entered Damascus,
and they went each to his own region.
And at that time, while al-Zahir and al-Afdal were encamped against Damascus,
Nur al-Din gathered his forces,
and took with him his cousin Qutb
